concept.name: Transactional Outbox Pattern
concept.tagline: Atomically persist domain changes and outbound events in one database transaction, then relay asynchronously to the message bus.

spark.summary: The outbox table stores events in the same DB transaction as business rows; a relay process publishes to Kafka/RabbitMQ with at-least-once delivery.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never “write DB then publish”—dual writes race crashes; outbox makes intent durable before transport.

concept.whyItMatters: It is the standard fix for “update order row and emit OrderCreated” consistency.
whenNotToUse: Fire-and-forget analytics with no consistency requirement
keyPoints: Same transaction for row + outbox insert

examples.title: Order placed event
examples.scenario: Insert order row and outbox record together.
examples.outcome: Relay publishes after commit; retries safe with idempotent consumers.

failureModes.name: Stuck relay
failureModes.mitigation: Lag alerts and dead-letter for poison payloads.

deepDive.markdownContent:
## Outbox relay

Durably record intent, then async publish.

relationships.description: Outbox is the reliable handoff to the event bus.
